decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. Gacek and Smoleń (2025) collected new empirical data from 75 Polish students across three groups (25 special vocational school students with mild intellectual disability, 25 mainstream vocational school chronological-age controls, and 25 primary school cognitive-ability-matched controls) to conceptually replicate Harter and Zigler (1974) across all four aspects of effectance motivation using tasks modeled on the original protocols: Puzzle Difficulty Task ('Puzzle Preference'), Maze Task ('Box Maze'), Choose-a-Door Task ('Pictorial Curiosity'), and Pegs and Pucks Task ('Graduated Pegs'). Group comparisons in Results (general linear, binomial, and ordered logistic regression models) found no statistically significant differences between the intellectual disability group and either control group on any of the four tasks, and the Discussion concludes that the results do not support the hypothesized group differences reported in Zigler and colleagues' original studies. The sole shipped row (1214, Zigler & Balla, 1972, 10.1037/h0032236) is a distinct original paper testing social reinforcement responsiveness ('Marble in the Hole' / Dice-Hole Task), and sibling missing target 1 (Yando & Zigler, 1971, 10.1037/h0030506) is a distinct paper testing outerdirectedness ('Sticker Game' / Sticker Task), so report equivalence does not apply.

decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. Gacek and Smoleń (2025) empirically re-tested Yando and Zigler's (1971) finding on outerdirectedness in problem-solving using a new sample of 75 participants across three groups (mild intellectual disability, chronological-age control, and mental-age/RSPM-matched control) on the Sticker Task, modeled directly on Yando and Zigler's (1971) 'Sticker Game'. In Results, a general linear model of the sum of imitated designs showed no statistically significant differences between the special vocational school group and either the mainstream vocational school group (p = .087, adjusted p = .339) or the primary school group (p = .067, adjusted p = .339, F(2, 72) = 1.40), leading the authors to conclude in the Discussion that their results disagree with the earlier studies by Zigler and colleagues. The sole shipped row (1214, Zigler & Balla, 1972, 10.1037/h0032236) tests social reinforcement responsiveness in a separate 1972 study, and sibling target 0 (Harter & Zigler, 1974, 10.1037/h0036049) tests effectance motivation in a separate 1974 study; report equivalence does not apply.

decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. Xu et al. (2024) recruited 600 Chinese general adults and conducted latent class analysis (LCA) to empirically re-test whether the four latent patterns of negative emotional eating (non-EE, EOE-EUE, EOE, and EUE) and their class differences identified in American and Chinese university students (Dixit et al., 2023; He et al., 2020) replicate in a general adult population, explicitly stating in both the introduction and conclusion previews that the study replicated and extended both Dixit et al. (2023) and He et al. (2020). Furthermore, Dixit et al. (2023) is the closer study in the replication chain that specifically proposed the future directions tested here (replicating the four patterns in a general, non-student population and examining emotion regulation differences across classes). (2023) (Appetite, 186, 106554, citedOrder 23) is an independent empirical article in an American university sample and is absent from the shipped rows. No DOI is printed for Dixit et al.
